notes: v2.5.15 - required update. A big release. CATIA remote viewing - the freezing had a structural cause and it is fixed: the machine's buffer of recently-sent packets held about 61 milliseconds of history while the round trip to the machine is 74-86 ms, so a request to resend a lost packet could never be answered in time. It now holds roughly half a second. A frozen picture behind healthy indicators now raises an alarm instead of reading green for nine minutes. The picture is no longer stretched, Escape goes to the remote machine instead of ending your session, Alt+F4 can no longer close your model, nothing draws on top of the model any more, and mouse movement is a frame quicker. Choosing the nearest machine no longer costs three quarters of a second on every Connect - a cold click is now 253 ms. Deleting a BOM item no longer strands its CAD file on the drive; measured against live data, 64 files across 1,020 deletions were being left behind, and all three faults behind that are fixed. 'Open in AOS' links in Teams keep working through an imminent network change. The wiki stops refusing to publish perfectly good pages, a lot classified as the wrong material can be corrected, and every requisition raised before AOS existed - twelve years of them - is readable again. Workforce planner - IMPORTANT: the numbers no longer change with the date range you have selected. Demand for a department on a given day was changing depending on whether you were looking at one month, three, six or twelve; on real project data 530 of 1,602 department-days disagreed across views, by as much as 74.6 hours a day, with one department reading 6.6 times higher in a narrow view than a wide one. Every view now returns the identical figure. Expect figures to come DOWN: if you have been planning from a one- or three-month view, the demand and utilisation you were reading were inflated, and anyone who made a staffing or scheduling decision on a short-range view should look at it again. Finished work is also no longer reported as a failure - a budget window in the past is history, not an error, and it stays editable; 'Impossible pace' no longer fires on work that is nearly done (a 120-hour window that was 34% loaded was being reported as needing 60 hours a day against a 32-hour ceiling, and now reads 10.9); the overtime allowance is read from where it is actually configured, so the 'needs overtime' level is reachable again; and AOS no longer claims something is impossible when it cannot know. 'Over capacity' now means one thing instead of six. Commercial value - a project can now record what it was sold for, with the exact calc-sheet revision it came from, who captured it and when, plus a full history of any correction. A value that was never captured says which of the reasons applies rather than showing a confident zero. Customer POs can carry the amount they authorise. Starting projects - 'Accept Quote & Create Project' is now 'Accept and Start Project'; a project can be started without a quote and quoted afterwards, which was previously a one-way door; Teams channels can be set up with the project. Operations Intelligence - Customer Requests and Careers move under External Relations, Quotes/Client PO/Projects/ECN are one Work group laid out to show how work flows, the tab bar has been rebuilt, and a job can be followed end to end from the first customer request through to the change notices raised against it. Every customer PO ever filed is now browsable - the review inbox showed 14 rows and the other 1,396 had no screen at all - and every review decision is recorded permanently. ECN gains a full lifecycle audit trail and its disposition emails are restored. Quotes gain a real REVISING state, a structured rejection reason and file provenance. Global Activity now reports change notices, pending items, file uploads across all eleven places AOS accepts them, and document version changes. This release also updates the database behind AOS, so please update as soon as you are prompted.
